about: Local state on a real filesystem (appendix A 41-44, 63, 65 and the plan's protection semantics N5). Each scenario states the starting files, the action and what must hold afterwards. All state lives under the skill's data/ (NAVER_BLOG_DATA_DIR in tests). Contexts are the query identity a handle or file is bound to: command, target, sort/type/kind, window, and the Naver account (current-user userId).

protection.fact: Every request runs inside one critical section under a cross-process lock: block check → command budget → 10-minute window → pacing → the request is reserved (logged) before it is sent → sent → classified → a block recorded before the lock is released. A process killed in flight has still spent its slot. Unreadable protection state is a block (fail closed).

scenarios.name: reserve-before-send
scenarios.action: one request whose sender is killed after the reservation
scenarios.after: requests.jsonl holds one entry {at, kind, n: 1}; the 10-minute window counts it

scenarios.name: command-budget
scenarios.action: a non-collecting command asks for its 11th request
scenarios.after: refused before sending: exit 8, stop_reason budget; 10 were sent

scenarios.name: collect-budget
scenarios.action: --limit above the command's default, a date window, --out or images: the 41st request
scenarios.after: refused: exit 8 budget; 40 sent. --limit at or below the default keeps the budget at 10

scenarios.name: window-full
scenarios.start: 120 logged requests in the last 600 s, the oldest 500 s ago
scenarios.after: refused before sending: exit 10 (not 5), stop_reason rate_window, the next allowed time = oldest + 600 s is stated; no block file is written

scenarios.name: window-slides
scenarios.start: 120 logged requests, the oldest 601 s ago
scenarios.after: sent

scenarios.name: pacing
scenarios.after: it waits until at least 0.5 s (+0-0.3 s) after the last; NAVER_BLOG_NO_PACING=1 skips the wait in tests

scenarios.name: 429-blocks-30-minutes
scenarios.after: blocked.json {reason rate_limit, blocked_at, expires_at = +1800}; the next command exits 5 without sending; after expiry requests resume on their own

scenarios.name: network-blocked-blocks-until-a-person
scenarios.action: current-user answers networkBlocked true (R18 decides its meaning before P3)
scenarios.after: blocked.json {reason network_blocked, expires_at null}; only a verified doctor --unblock clears it

scenarios.name: unreadable-state-fails-closed
scenarios.after: refused: exit 5 (state unreadable); nothing sent

scenarios.name: two-processes
scenarios.action: two processes send 5 requests each at once
scenarios.after: 10 entries, never two requests inside one pacing gap; the lock serializes them

scenarios.name: unblock-verifies-first
scenarios.after: one current-user check is sent while the block stands; only a logged-in, not networkBlocked answer for the same account clears it, and only the block read at the start (a newer one written meanwhile stays). The 10-minute window is never cleared

scenarios.name: unblock-refused
scenarios.action: doctor --unblock while current-user still says networkBlocked true
scenarios.after: exit 5; the block stays

scenarios.name: unblock-interrupted
scenarios.action: doctor --unblock killed during its check, or the check fails
scenarios.after: the block stays

scenarios.name: recent-usage
scenarios.after: reports requests in the last 10 minutes, hour and day, read from requests.jsonl (observation only; a broken line is skipped)

session.fact: Who the browser is logged in as (current-user userId) is cached for 12 hours, because asking costs a request. A post page names the viewer, which refreshes the cache for free. A different account invalidates every handle (they are page numbers into one account's view). viewer identifiers other than the blog id (idNo, baUserKey) are never stored.

scenarios.name: cold
scenarios.action: a command that needs the account
scenarios.after: one current-user request; session.json {account (userId), blog_no, read_at}

scenarios.name: warm
scenarios.after: no request

scenarios.name: stale
scenarios.after: one current-user request

scenarios.name: post-refreshes
scenarios.action: post reads a page whose userId names the same account
scenarios.after: read_at renewed, no request

scenarios.name: account-changed
scenarios.start: session for account A and handles
scenarios.after: session for B; every saved handle is refused (exit 2, rerun the original command)

scenarios.name: logged-out
scenarios.after: exit 4; the session is not overwritten

handles.fact: A handle is a monotonic number, reserved and fsynced in the counter before its file is written (an interruption leaves a gap, never a reused number), bound to its query context and the Naver account, format-versioned, and kept 24 hours. It carries the unshown tail and what a continuation needs (comment handles carry blog_no and the total, saving one request).

scenarios.name: save-and-load
scenarios.action: save(context X, state) then load(n, X)
scenarios.after: the state comes back

scenarios.name: other-context
scenarios.after: exit 2: belongs to another command, target, order or account

scenarios.name: expired
scenarios.action: load a handle saved 25 h ago
scenarios.after: exit 2: expired, rerun the original command; the file is cleaned

scenarios.name: old-format
scenarios.action: load a handle whose format is not the current one (e.g. one written by the old skill)
scenarios.after: exit 2, the file is not changed

scenarios.name: never-reused
scenarios.action: save after the counter was reserved but the file write failed
scenarios.after: the next handle skips that number

scenarios.name: cleaning-keeps-the-counter
scenarios.action: handle files expire and are removed
scenarios.after: the counter stays, so numbers never restart

collection.fact: --out NDJSON: a header (format, context), then records, each page closed by a page marker (state, ids, n, stop_reason). Only complete pages are trusted: on resume the tail after the last marker is dropped and read again; a damaged line before a later marker is an integrity failure. Duplicates by id are not written twice. The file is opened without following a symlink, mode 0600, locked without waiting. A file for another query or format is refused before any byte changes. An empty page is committed too, so the state moves on. A finished file (exhausted, window_reached, not_paginable, server_capped, pagination_stalled) reads nothing; a file stopped by budget or rate_window is not finished — the same command resumes it. post --out writes a failed section as its own row, so the file never reads later as a post without comments.

scenarios.name: header
scenarios.after: one header line with X and the format; mode 0600

scenarios.name: commit
scenarios.after: A, B, then {kind: page, state: S, ids: [A, B], n: 2, stop_reason}

scenarios.name: torn-tail
scenarios.start: a committed page, then half a record
scenarios.after: the half record is dropped; resuming starts from the last state

scenarios.name: damaged-middle
scenarios.start: a broken line, then a page marker
scenarios.after: exit 2 integrity failure; the file is unchanged

scenarios.name: other-query
scenarios.after: exit 2; unchanged

scenarios.name: old-skill-file
scenarios.start: a file written by the current skill (header without format)
scenarios.after: exit 2; unchanged byte for byte

scenarios.name: symlink
scenarios.after: exit 2; the target untouched

scenarios.name: empty-page
scenarios.after: a page marker with n 0 and S2

scenarios.name: budget-is-not-done
scenarios.start: a file whose last page says budget
scenarios.after: it continues from the saved state

scenarios.name: after-is-refused
scenarios.after: exit 2 before any request

images.fact: Downloaded photos live under data/images/ and are removed 24 hours after they were saved, by the skill itself; nobody needs to delete them. A saved name is derived by the skill (never from the URL path), so a URL cannot write outside data/images/. The command prints each path so the model can Read it.

scenarios.name: save
scenarios.action: save image bytes for post P, number N
scenarios.after: a file under data/images/ whose name the skill chose; its path is returned

scenarios.name: ttl
scenarios.after: the old file is gone

scenarios.name: escape
scenarios.action: a URL path holding ../ or an absolute path
scenarios.after: the file still lands under data/images/ (the name never comes from the URL)
